title: Reindexing preserves circuit depth
statement: Let $m,m'$ be natural numbers, let $c$ be a Boolean circuit on $m$ variables, and let $f$ map the $m$ input indices to the $m'$ input indices. Replacing each input index of $c$ by its image under $f$ preserves depth.
hypotheses_covered: $c$ is a Boolean circuit on $m$ variables
replaced:
Let $c$ be a Boolean circuit on $m$ variables and let $f : \mathrm{Fin}\,m \to
\mathrm{Fin}\,m'$ be any map of variable indices. Then re-indexing $c$ along $f$ leaves
its depth unchanged: $\mathrm{depth}(\mathrm{reidx}(c, f)) = \mathrm{depth}(c)$.
